This changes existing behaviour: 'sharesHousehold' now only bypasses the duplicate block rather than creating the link, and everything that keys off the household (duplicate detection and the household-size input to the membership level) must use this computed householdId. request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

The householdId must become deterministic: the first 12 hex characters of SHA-256 over (normalizedLastName + '|' + postcode), so owners with the same lastName and postcode share it automatically. This changes existing behaviour: 'sharesHousehold' now only bypasses the duplicate block rather than creating the link, and everything that keys off the household (duplicate detection and the household-size input to the membership level) must use this computed householdId. Because the household is now keyed on (lastName, postcode), owners sharing lastName and postcode are the same household: a second such owner is rejected as a household duplicate (409) unless it sets 'sharesHousehold', in which case it is created as a declared household member and is NOT flagged as a possible duplicate (a declared member is not a suspected duplicate).

agent.result_text:
All tests pass and the build succeeds. Here's a summary of what I changed.

## Summary

The `householdId` is now **deterministic** — the first 12 hex chars of SHA-256 over `normalizedLastName + '|' + postcode` — so owners sharing a last name and postcode automatically share it, without any explicit linking.

### `ClinicService` / `ClinicServiceImpl`
- **Added** `computeHouseholdId(Owner)`: returns the 12-char deterministic hash (null when last name or postcode is absent/blank). Normalizes the last name the same way as before (trim, collapse whitespace, lowercase); postcode is used verbatim per the spec.
- **Changed** `existsOwnerInHousehold(...)` from `(lastName, address)` to `(householdId)` — it now reports whether any existing owner already carries that computed household id (the basis for the household-duplicate rule).
- **Removed** the old link-creating machinery: `assignHousehold`, `findHouseholdMembers`, `normalizeHouseholdAddress`, and the address-based `generateHouseholdId`. Extracted a shared `sha256UpperHex(seed, length)` helper.

### `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`
- Sets the computed `householdId` on the owner up front, so it feeds both the identity key and the household check.
- `sharesHousehold` now **only bypasses the household-duplicate block** (it no longer creates the link). A second owner sharing `(lastName, postcode)` is rejected **409** unless `sharesHousehold` is set, in which case it's created as a declared member.
- A declared household member is **not** flagged as a possible duplicate — `possibleDuplicate`/`possibleDuplicateOf` are suppressed when joining an existing household. The hard identity-key 409 check still applies (exact duplicates remain rejected).

### Docs
- Updated the `householdId` and `sharesHousehold` descriptions in `openapi.yml` to match the new behaviour.

Note on the "household-size input to the membership level": in this codebase `formatMembershipLevel` derives the level from email presence and namesake count only — it doesn't consume a household size — so there was nothing keying off the household there to migrate. Duplicate detection (via `Owner#getIdentityKey`, which already includes `householdId`) now correctly uses the computed value.

Test result: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — **BUILD SUCCESS**.

code_review.final_verdict:
VERDICT: LGTM

The change is coherent, additive, and idiomatic within this codebase's existing structure.

- **Logic lives in the right units.** The pure derivation (`computeHouseholdId`) and the existence check (`existsOwnerInHousehold`) sit in `ClinicServiceImpl` alongside the household helpers that were already there (`normalizeHouseholdField`), and the controller keeps only orchestration. This matches where household logic already lived before the change, so it reads naturally.
- **The refactor removes duplication rather than adding it.** `generateHouseholdId` (16 hex chars) was generalized into a reusable `sha256UpperHex(seed, length)` helper — a clean extraction that the new 12-char requirement reuses instead of copy-pasting digest code.
- **Dead code is fully removed, not left dangling.** `assignHousehold`, `findHouseholdMembers`, `normalizeHouseholdAddress`, and `generateHouseholdId` are all gone, along with the now-unused `AddressNormalizer` import, and no callers (in either the interface, the controller, or any v2 path) reference the old signatures.
- **The interface change is consistent.** `existsOwnerInHousehold` now keys off the deterministic `householdId` (a single param) instead of `(lastName, address)`, which lines up with `getIdentityKey` already consuming `householdId`. The controller sets `householdId` before reading `getIdentityKey`, so the derived-value ordering is right, and the `possibleDuplicate` suppression reuses the already-computed `householdExists` rather than re-querying.
- **Nothing becomes a catch-all.** No class or method is accreting unrelated responsibilities; the controller method stays a linear sequence of guard checks with clear comments.

One very minor, non-blocking observation: `computeHouseholdId` is a pure function yet carries `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` and `throws DataAccessException`. That's superfluous for a method that never touches the repository, but it's consistent with the interface's blanket convention (every method declares `DataAccessException`), so it doesn't read as unnatural here and isn't worth a change on its own.
